questions.q: What does the summary claim about high-intensity workouts?
a: They produce better results in less time than steady routines
They are safe only for experienced athletes
They should be done five times a week
They build endurance but not strength
questions.why: Putting pressure on muscle tissue kickstarts metabolism and builds endurance.

questions.q: Which downsides of jogging does the summary mention?
a: Weak knees, spinal degeneration and arrhythmia
Muscle loss, low energy and poor sleep
Dehydration, cramps and joint swelling
Shortness of breath and high blood pressure
questions.why: The summary says cardio has benefits but also these risks.

questions.q: Which five moves make up the Big Five routine?
a: Pulldowns, leg presses, seated rows, chest presses, overhead presses
Squats, deadlifts, bench presses, pull-ups, lunges
Running, cycling, rowing, swimming, jumping
Curls, dips, flyes, shrugs, calf raises
questions.why: These five resistance moves target all the major muscle groups.

questions.q: Why is cardio inefficient for losing weight, according to the summary?
a: A pound of fat holds 3,500 calories; an hour of jogging burns about 200
Cardio raises appetite more than it burns energy
Cardio builds fat around the muscles
The body stops burning calories after 20 minutes
questions.why: The mismatch between calories stored and calories burned makes exercise alone ineffective.

questions.q: How much extra energy does each pound of muscle burn per day?
a: About 100 calories
About 20 calories
About 500 calories
About 1,000 calories
questions.why: The summary offers this as a rule of thumb for why building muscle helps with fat loss.
